valuation_method: 10-year enterprise owner-cash model with explicit reverse-expectations test

reverse_expectations.interpretation: At the current price, a defensible valuation requires roughly 17%-20% annual revenue compounding for a decade while owner-cash economics mature into the mid/high-20s. This is feasible for a category winner but is not a low-expectations setup.

bear.narrative: AI timing demand normalizes sharply, Renesas integration returns disappoint, quartz/integrated alternatives cap share gains and dilution/expense remain elevated.

base.narrative: SiTime sustains category leadership, Renesas cross-sell works, gross margins remain >=65%, timing content per AI/physical-AI system expands and SBC normalizes materially.

bull.narrative: Precision Timing becomes a dominant semiconductor infrastructure layer; SiTime wins broad clock/resonator/oscillator/software content across AI, optical, auto and edge, with durable premium economics.

subjective_probability_example.warning: Subjective research aid, not a target price or trade instruction.

permanent_loss_case: A combination of AI-capex normalization, failure to earn an adequate return on the ~$4.0B Renesas purchase price, quartz/competitor/in-house integration preserving sufficient performance, Titan adoption stalling, high SBC and share issuance persisting, and a semiconductor-duration multiple reset can produce a large permanent equity loss despite corporate solvency.
terminal_value_warning: Terminal value is dominant in long-duration scenarios. Values are highly sensitive to assumed owner-cash margin, duration and terminal multiple; purchase accounting amortization and SBC normalization remain unresolved.
